name: Extreme wide shot
use: Subject tiny in a vast environment; establishes scale.

name: Wide shot
use: Whole body plus surroundings; shows movement through space.

name: Full shot
use: Head to toe; best for dance and athletic form.

name: Medium shot
use: Waist up; gestures and upper-body action.

name: Medium close-up
use: Chest up; performance and emotion.

name: Close-up
use: Face, hands or a single detail of the movement.

name: Extreme close-up
use: A tiny detail fills the frame: an eye, a fingertip, a feather.

name: Two-shot
use: Two subjects in frame; partner and conversation movement.

name: Over-the-shoulder
use: Framed past one subject toward another.

name: Silhouette
use: Subject reduced to a dark shape against bright light; pure body line.

name: Eye-level
use: Neutral and intimate; at the subject’s own eye height.

name: Low angle
use: Looking up; makes movement feel powerful and heroic.

name: High angle
use: Looking down; shows patterns and vulnerability.

name: Top-down / bird’s-eye
use: Directly overhead; reveals formation and floor patterns.

name: Worm’s-eye
use: From the ground looking straight up.

name: Ground level
use: Lens inches above the floor; feet, paws and impact.

name: Dutch angle
use: Tilted horizon; tension and disorientation.

name: Locked-off static
use: Camera does not move; the subject provides all motion.

name: Pan
use: Horizontal rotation from a fixed point to follow or reveal.

name: Whip pan
use: Fast snap rotation with motion blur; energetic transitions.

name: Tilt up
use: Vertical rotation upward; reveals height or rises from feet to face.

name: Tilt down
use: Vertical rotation downward; descends a subject.

name: Camera roll
use: Camera rotates on the lens axis; dreamlike or disorienting.

name: Dolly in / push in
use: Camera physically moves toward the subject; builds intensity with parallax.

name: Dolly out / pull back
use: Camera retreats; reveals context or isolates the subject.

name: Push past
use: Glides forward past a foreground object into the action.

name: Truck
use: Camera slides sideways while facing the same direction.

name: Pedestal up
use: Whole camera rises vertically with the lens level.

name: Pedestal down
use: Whole camera lowers vertically with the lens level.

name: Side tracking
use: Camera travels parallel to the subject; shows speed in profile.

name: Follow from behind
use: Camera trails the subject; immersive journeys.

name: Leading / reverse tracking
use: Camera moves backward in front of the subject; faces and forward momentum.

name: Low tracking
use: Ground-level travel alongside feet, paws or wheels.

name: Arc
use: Shallow curve around the subject; adds dimension.

name: Orbit
use: Full circle around the subject; hero reveals.

name: Low orbit
use: Circling from below; power moves and breaking.

name: Crane up
use: Rising arc from the subject to a wide reveal.

name: Crane down
use: Descending arc from above into the action.

name: Jib sweep
use: Short crane arm sweeping across a scene.

name: Cable cam
use: Camera flies on wires above a field or stage.

name: Steadicam
use: Smooth walking camera; long flowing takes.

name: Gimbal
use: Stabilized but agile; chases through tight spaces.

name: Handheld
use: Organic sway; documentary realism.

name: Snorricam
use: Rig strapped to the body; face locked while the world lurches.

name: First-person POV
use: Through the subject’s own eyes.

name: Helmet cam
use: Action-camera POV mounted on a helmet.

name: Chest mount
use: Camera on the chest; hands and board in frame.

name: Oner / long take
use: Unbroken take following the action through space.

name: Vehicle interior
use: Rigged inside a vehicle on the driver or passenger.

name: Drone rise
use: Ascends to reveal the landscape around the subject.

name: Drone top-down
use: Directly overhead from altitude; patterns and formations.

name: Drone orbit
use: Circles the subject from the air.

name: Drone chase
use: Flies alongside or behind fast-moving subjects.

name: FPV drone
use: Agile first-person drone; dives and fly-throughs.

name: Zoom in
use: Optical magnification toward the subject; no parallax.

name: Zoom out
use: Optical pull back to reveal context.

name: Crash zoom
use: Violent snap zoom for punchy emphasis.

name: Dolly zoom
use: Dolly and zoom in opposite directions; background warps.

name: Rack focus
use: Focus shifts between foreground and background.

name: Split diopter
use: Near and far planes both in focus.

name: Telephoto
use: Compressed perspective; wildlife and sport from a distance.

name: Ultra-wide
use: Exaggerated perspective close to the action.

name: Fisheye
use: Curved extreme wide angle; skate and street culture.

name: Macro
use: Tiny subjects magnified; texture and detail.

name: Probe lens
use: Long thin macro lens that moves through tiny spaces.

name: Tilt-shift
use: Narrow focus band makes scenes look like toy models.

name: Anamorphic
use: 2.39:1 frame, oval bokeh and horizontal flares.

name: Slow motion
use: Movement slowed about 10x; elegance and detail.

name: High-speed (Phantom)
use: Extreme slow motion; impacts, splashes, wingbeats.

name: Speed ramp
use: Shifts between real time and slow motion at the peak.

name: Time-lapse
use: Compresses hours into seconds.

name: Hyperlapse
use: Moving time-lapse traveling through space.

name: Bullet time
use: Action frozen while the camera sweeps around it.

name: Freeze frame
use: Action stops at the peak moment.

name: Reverse motion
use: Played backward for surreal or comic effect.

name: Seamless loop
use: Last frame matches the first; endless social loops.

name: Underwater
use: Camera fully submerged.

name: Split-level
use: Lens straddles the waterline: above and below at once.

name: Hero shot
use: The subject or product shown at its most powerful.

name: Motion control
use: Precise repeatable robotic move; high-end commercials.

name: Turntable 360
use: Subject rotates on a turntable before a fixed camera.

name: Flat lay
use: Overhead tabletop composition; food and product.

name: Beauty shot
use: Flawless skin, glow and texture in soft wrap-around light.

name: Packshot finish
use: Clean product-forward ending frame with room for a logo.

name: Lifestyle
use: Real-life context; aspirational but authentic.

name: UGC selfie-style
use: User-generated look; handheld phone authenticity.

name: Testimonial
use: Subject speaking to camera with sincerity.

name: Unboxing
use: Hands open and reveal the product.

name: Product demo
use: Shows exactly how the product is used.

name: Split screen / before-after
use: Two states side by side.

name: Match-cut transition
use: Movement or shape bridges two scenes invisibly.

name: Reveal
use: Foreground wipe or movement reveals the subject.

name: Stop motion
use: Frame-by-frame animated look.

name: Vertical 9:16
use: Composed for phones: centered subject, vertical motion.
